To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tetraspanin CD9 interacts with transmembrane transforming growth factor-α, regulates the conversion of transmembrane transforming to growth factor-α to soluble growth factor, regulates transforming growth factor- α–inducible activation of the EGF receptor, and regulates the proliferative effect of the transforming growth factor- alpha–induced EGF receptor activation.
CD9 associates with transmembrane transforming growth factor-α, regulates its ligand-induced activation and signaling, and modulates cell growth.
the tetraspanin Cd 9 regulates TGF-α-induced EGFR activation and cell proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), which is frequently overexpressed in human carcinomas.
the role of CD9 and TGF-α, two proteins that are often expressed in the same cell types.
the role of tetraspanins in cell adhesion and signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD9 regulates transmembrane Tgf-α–mediated signaling by modulating TGF-α expression and EGFR activation.
CD9 is a novel modulator of TGF- α/EGFR signaling.
CD9 is a novel transmembrane TFG-α binding partner that regulates the ligand-induced EGFR activation and cell proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD9-TGF-α interaction is a new regulatory mechanism for TGF-α/EGFR signaling.
the tetraspanin Cd-9 regulates transmembrane Tgfa-induced EGF receptor activation and cell proliferation.
the tetraspanin, CD9, regulates the ligand-induced activation, and thus the function, of the EGFR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD9 regulates transmembrane Tgf-α–induced EGFr activation and cell proliferation, and that the association of transmembrane with CD9 is a critical determinant of the Tgf-α signaling outcome.
transmembrane growth factors can be regulated by their association with other transmembrane proteins, which can have important biological effects on the growth factor–induced cell responses.
the association of transmembrane growth factors with tetraspanins can regulate the ligand-induced activation, and the functional outcome of these ligands.
